text: dsh-kubectl-guard 是一款面向 DSH Web 的 Kubernetes 命令策略插件。它接入 shell 工具执行前的流程，识别 kubectl 和 k 命令，并依据当前 kubeconfig context 判断操作类型。读取类命令以及配置为本地的集群操作会放行；非本地集群上的可恢复写入会请求确认，删除等不可逆操作会拒绝。它还识别 dry-run、命令链和多种 context 指定方式，适合希望在 DSH 会话中管理 Kubernetes 集群的用户。配置可调整本地 context 模式、命令别名、受检查工具和是否显示 context 名称。

dsh-kubectl-guard is a DSH Web plugin that checks kubectl and k shell commands against the selected Kubernetes context. Reads and configured local contexts pass; recoverable writes to other clusters ask for approval, while irreversible operations are denied. It handles dry runs and chained commands.
想让 DSH 在操作 Kubernetes 集群前先区分本地和生产环境。
DSH 里执行 kubectl 删除命令时，能不能直接拦下来？
我希望集群写入操作先弹出确认，再交给 shell 执行。
让 DSH 自动放行 kubectl 查询，但对变更操作进行处理。
如何按 kubeconfig 当前 context 判断 kubectl 命令的目标集群？
我想把 minikube 和 kind 集群设为无需确认的本地环境。
Can DSH ask me before running kubectl changes against a remote cluster?
I want destructive Kubernetes commands blocked outside my local contexts.
dsh-kubectl-guard 的功能「本地集群例外」：通过 localContexts 配置精确名称或带星号的模式来识别本地 context。kubectl 命令解析出的 context 命中这些模式时，写入操作也会直接放行。
dsh-kubectl-guard 的功能「写入确认」：对非本地集群上的可恢复写操作返回 ask 决策，由 DSH 工具执行流程请求用户确认。未知动词也按需确认处理。
dsh-kubectl-guard 的功能「不可逆操作拒绝」：识别 delete、drain 和 evict 等操作，并在目标不是已配置的本地集群时返回拒绝结果。
dsh-kubectl-guard 的功能「目标 context 解析」：按显式 --context、--kubeconfig、命令内 KUBECONFIG 和环境配置解析目标 context，再用于本地或非本地分类。

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) policy plugin that gates `kubectl` by kubeconfig context.

Irreversible verbs against a non-local cluster are denied outright. Recoverable writes ask first. Reads and local clusters are untouched.
dsh-kubectl-guard README · dsh-kubectl-guard：It registers no tools of its own — it inspects the `command` argument of shell tool calls, so it covers whatever the agent runs.

dsh-kubectl-guard README · Install：Requires [pnpm](https://pnpm.io), which `dsh plugin` shells out to.

**From npm:**

```
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-kubectl-guard
```

**From source**, if you want to hack on it:

```
git clone https://github.com/gengwg/dsh-kubectl-guard
cd dsh-kubectl-guard
dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD"
```

Either way, activation is automatic: the package declares `dsh.bundle`, so
`dsh plugin add` joins it to the profile's bundle stack. Restart dsh to load it.

dsh-kubectl-guard README · Install：Upgrading from 0.1.x, which installed as a plain dependency: delete the manual
insert entry from `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`. Bundle and user
patch layers both apply, so leaving it in loads the guard twice.

dsh-kubectl-guard README · Examples：Nothing to invoke. Ask the agent to do its normal work; the guard sits in the
tool pipeline and inspects the shell command before it runs.

Blocked, with the cluster name replaced by a per-session pseudonym:

```
> delete the stuck nginx pod

Error: kubectl-guard: 'delete' is irreversible and ctx#4be1f92a is not a local
cluster. Denied.

Asked, so you approve it in the UI before it runs:

```
> roll out the new deployment

dsh-kubectl-guard README · Examples：kubectl-guard: 'apply' writes to ctx#4be1f92a, which is not a local cluster.
[approve] [deny]

Untouched, because reads are not gated:

```
> what pods are failing in kube-system?

kubectl get pods -n kube-system --field-selector=status.phase!=Running
NAME         READY   STATUS             RESTARTS

Untouched, because the context is local:

```
> wipe the test namespace on my kind cluster

kubectl --context kind-dev delete ns test
namespace "test" deleted

dsh-kubectl-guard README · Examples：Dry runs are reads, so they pass and give the agent a way to show you a change
before asking for it:

```
kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f deploy.yaml     # allowed
kubectl apply -f deploy.yaml                      # asks
```

Turn the guard off for one session without editing config:

```
dsh web --patch <(echo '- id: kubectl-guard
  disabled: true')
```

dsh-kubectl-guard README · Behavior：| Command | Non-local context | Local context |
|---|---|---|
| `get`, `describe`, `logs`, `top` | allow | allow |
| `auth can-i` | allow | allow |
| `auth reconcile` | ask | allow |
| `config use-context`, other mutating `config` subcommands | ask | ask |
| `apply`, `patch`, `scale`, `exec` | ask | allow |
| `delete`, `drain`, `evict` | deny | allow |
| `scale --replicas=0` | deny | allow |
| `apply --prune` | deny | allow |
| `replace --force` | deny | allow |
| `apply --dry-run=server` | allow | allow |
dsh-kubectl-guard README · Behavior：A context is local only if it matches `localContexts`. Everything else, including a kubeconfig that cannot be read, is treated as production.

dsh-kubectl-guard README · Behavior：The context is resolved the way the shell would resolve it: an explicit
`--context` wins, then `--kubeconfig`, then a `KUBECONFIG=` assignment written
inline on the same command line, then the ambient environment. That last case
matters -- without it, `KUBECONFIG=/path/to/prod kubectl delete ...` would be
judged against whatever your shell happened to point at.

dsh-kubectl-guard README · Config：```yaml
config:
  localContexts: [minikube, 'kind-*', docker-desktop]
  binaries: [kubectl, k]
  guardedTools: [bash, pwsh]

`showContextNames` is off by default: blocked-command messages go to the model, and therefore to the LLM provider. With it off the model sees a stable per-session pseudonym like `ctx#4be1f92a` instead of your cluster's name.

dsh-kubectl-guard README · Failing closed：A gate that can be talked around is worse than none. Anything unparseable — `sh -c`, command substitution, an unterminated quote — is treated as a mutation: denied if the text contains an irreversible verb, asked otherwise. An unknown verb asks rather than allows.

dsh-kubectl-guard README · What this is not：This gates a cooperative agent, not an adversary. It reads the command string
the agent asked to run, so anything that hides the binary name from that string
defeats it by construction -- `$KUBECTL delete ...` with the name only in the
environment, a shell alias resolved at runtime, a base64 round-trip.

dsh-kubectl-guard README · What this is not：Indirection that still contains the literal name is caught: `K=kubectl; $K
delete pod foo` is denied, because any `$` expansion alongside a mention of a
guarded binary makes the command opaque, and opaque plus an irreversible verb
is a denial. But treat the guard as a seatbelt against a confused agent, not a
sandbox against a hostile one. If you need the stronger property, take the
credential away rather than filtering the command.

dsh-kubectl-guard README · Limitations：- Only `kubectl`. helm, argocd and flux are not covered; the verb table is data, so adding them is an edit to `src/verbs.js`.
- Pass-through wrappers (`sudo`, `time`, `nice`, ...) are seen through, but only until a bare-token wrapper argument: `timeout 30 kubectl delete ...` is not gated, because `30` ends the wrapper chain.
- `current-context` is read with a line-anchored regex, not a YAML parser. Unreadable or unmatched means production, so the failure direction is safe.
- The pseudonym salt is per-process: ids are stable within a session, not across restarts.
- Guards are synchronous, so the deny path does no I/O beyond a cached `readFileSync`.

npm test
